import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    p_values = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, col], feats.x[feats.y==0, col])
        p_values.append(p_val)
    
    # If no feature is significantly associated, return empty design
    if all(p > 0.05 for p in p_values):
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select features with p < 0.05 and not highly correlated
    selected_ids = []
    excluded = set()
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if p_values[i] < 0.05 and fid not in excluded:
            selected_ids.append(fid)
            # Mark correlated features as excluded
            for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids):
                if i != j and fid2 not in excluded:
                    col1 = feats.column(fid)
                    col2 = feats.column(fid2)
                    corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0,1]
                    if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                        excluded.add(fid2)
    
    # If no features left after filtering, return empty design
    if not selected_ids:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Fit logistic regression to check for interaction effects
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_ids]]
    model = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
    model.fit(X, feats.y)
    
    # Calculate weights based on coefficients
    weights = dict(zip(selected_ids, model.coef_[0]))
    
    # Check for interactions among top features
    top_features = sorted(selected_ids, key=lambda f: abs(weights[f]), reverse=True)[:5]
    products = []
    
    # Add pairwise products for top features
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            products.append((top_features[i], top_features[j]))
    
    # Return final design
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(top_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]),
        columns=tuple(selected_ids),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=weights
    )
